slides.title: Signed-out Session lifecycle
slides.subtitle: Start a Session, survive a nonce challenge, renew it before it expires
slides.notes: Every interaction a personal agent has with a company happens inside a Session. This example starts one signed out, meets the company's DPoP nonce challenge on the way, and renews the Session before its token expires.

slides.title: Why start signed out
slides.statement: The company recognises the **same user** across visits, without learning **who** they are.
slides.notes: A signed-out Session gives the company a stable, pairwise context: the same user ID every time this agent comes back for this user, and a different one at every other company. Public questions and a conversation can start here, and continue later through sign-in.

slides.title: Who takes part

columns.heading: PAP host
columns.content: Your code. It asks for the Session and keeps every credential out of the model's reach.

columns.heading: Reactor contributions
columns.content: The **signer** makes assertions; the **DPoP provider** makes proofs. Both are replaceable.

columns.heading: Company
columns.content: Its authorization server issues the Session Token, and may demand a fresh **nonce**.

slides.notes: Three parties: the host, which is your application; the Reactor contributions that hold the keys, a signer for assertions and a DPoP provider for proofs; and the company's authorization server.

slides.title: Starting the Session

items.title: Sign
items.detail: A fresh Session assertion and client assertion

items.title: Prove
items.detail: A DPoP proof, no nonce yet

items.title: Ask
items.detail: JWT bearer grant at the token endpoint

slides.notes: The host signs two assertions, proves possession of its key with a DPoP proof, and asks the token endpoint for a Session. This company answers use_dpop_nonce: it wants proofs bound to a nonce it issued, so no proof can be made in advance.

slides.title: The retry

items.title: Sign again
items.detail: New assertions: a jti is never reused

items.title: Prove again
items.detail: A new proof carrying the nonce

items.title: Signed-out Session
items.detail: A DPoP Session Token, bound to the key

slides.notes: The retry is not a resend. Assertions and proofs each carry a unique identifier the company refuses to see twice, so the host signs fresh ones and puts the nonce in the new proof. The answer is a DPoP-bound Session Token: useless to anyone who copies it without the key.

slides.title: The whole exchange
slides.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as PAP host
  participant C as Company
  H->>C: Start Session (assertions, proof)
  C-->>H: use_dpop_nonce
  H->>C: Retry (fresh assertions, proof with nonce)
  C-->>H: Session Token (signed out)
  Note over H,C: Before expiry
  H->>C: Renew (fresh assertions, fresh proof)
  C-->>H: Renewed Session Token
slides.notes: Here is the whole exchange at once: the challenge, the retry, and later the renewal of the same Session before its token expires.

slides.title: Renewing, not restarting
items: Before expiry, the host renews **the same Session**
Fresh assertions and a fresh proof, every time
The conversation and its context carry on
A Session that has ended answers an error: start a new one
slides.notes: Renewal keeps the same Session, so the conversational state the company holds carries on. Every renewal still signs fresh assertions and a fresh proof.

slides.title: What stays where
slides.notes: None of the credentials reach the model. Tokens, assertions, proofs, pairwise subjects and nonces stay in host code and protected storage; the model sees the Session's status, its scopes, and nothing it could leak.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples run this lifecycle against a deterministic company
slides.notes: The example's company always answers one nonce challenge, so the retry path is exercised on every run. Production code uses the same SessionClient over real HTTPS, with managed Reactor contributions.
